business_problem: Becoming a cloud-first organization and embracing the possibilities of generative AI offered Holcim the opportunity to enhance agility and operational efficiency. By addressing the limitations of traditional data centers, Holcim wanted to position itself to deliver more innovative, scalable services and foster sustainable growth.
solution_summary: Holcim is transforming its business with the cloud and empowered its staff to innovate by launching a cloud upskilling program, the I&O Skills Guild. Holcim is a global leader in innovative and sustainable building solutions. Based in Europe and operating in more than 70 countries, Holcim’s 63,448 employees are driven by the purpose of building progress for people and the planet across regions and improving living standards for all. As part of Holcim’s vision of maintaining industry leadership and being ready for whatever the future holds, it embarked on a cloud-first strategy, modernizing its infrastructure and business applications and utilizing generative AI to drive innovation and enhance efficiency. Leaders at Holcim recognized that, in the face of rapid technological change, the shift was about more than just new infrastructure and applications: Holcim would also need to build internal cloud expertise and start a cultural shift toward collaboration and innovation.
business_outcome: The I&O Skills Guild has been instrumental in Holcim’s successful cloud transformation, and the new culture of collaboration and innovation quickly delivered tangible business outcomes with the AWS Cloud and generative AI. One group of employees, many of whose members had taken part in the program, developed Omnivore, an AI-powered invoice processing system powered by large language models. Key reported metrics include participation rate in the I&O Skills Guild 85%; 85% growth in teams trained on AWS in just 1 year; growth in teams trained on AWS in just 1 year 38%.

The I&O Skills Guild helped us build AI-powered solutions that have reduced 90 percent of manual processing, freeing up focus for strategic priorities.
In the first 2 years, more than 50 training sessions were delivered on topics ranging from generative AI and machine learning to data engineering and cloud security.
The program achieved impressive engagement, with an 85 percent participation rate and a 38 percent increase globally in teams trained in AWS services.
